question: Why do Nordic countries top the happiness rankings?
title: nordic happiness
hook: What keeps a single region at the top of the global happiness charts?
answer: Nordic nations dominate global well-being rankings, securing five of the top six spots in the world in 2025.

stats.label: Nordic countries ranking in the global top six
years Finland has held the top global spot
greater impact from low corruption views than globally

followups: How did Costa Rica reach fourth place without being in Europe?
Why has Norway fallen behind its Nordic neighbors in recent years?
What explains Iceland's rapid rise in happiness since 2011?
body:
## nordic countries crowd the top

Five of the top six spots in the global happiness rankings belong to Nordic nations (WHR 2026). Finland leads the world with a life evaluation score of **7.8** on a ten-point scale, followed by Iceland at 7.5 and Denmark at 7.5 (WHR 2026).

Sweden ranks fifth at 7.3 and Norway is sixth at 7.2 (WHR 2026). Only Costa Rica, ranking fourth with a score of **7.4**, interrupts what would otherwise be a clean sweep of the highest tiers (WHR 2026).

```chart
{"type": "bar", "title": "Nordic nations dominate the top of the global rankings", "y_label": "life evaluation score", "unit": "", "labels": ["Finland", "Iceland", "Denmark", "Costa Rica", "Sweden", "Norway"], "series": [{"name": "score", "data": [7.8, 7.5, 7.5, 7.4, 7.3, 7.2]}], "highlight": "Finland", "note": "Scores on a 0 to 10 scale for the year 2025."}
```

## wealth and trust go with higher scores

The happiness advantage in these countries is clear, with Nordic nations averaging an overall life evaluation of 7.5, compared to an average of **5.6** for the other 142 countries surveyed (WHR 2026). High national income per person is the largest single contributor, accounting for 2.0 points of the average Nordic score compared to 1.5 points in other nations (WHR 2026).

Social systems also play a massive role, as having someone to count on in times of trouble explains **1.6 points** of the Nordic score compared to 1.2 points globally (WHR 2026).

The sharpest relative contrast appears in how citizens view their institutions, with low corruption explaining **0.4 points** in the Nordic region compared to 0.1 points elsewhere (WHR 2026). Personal freedom to make life choices adds another 1.1 points to the Nordic total, compared to 0.9 points globally (WHR 2026).

```chart
{"type": "bar", "title": "Social trust and wealth set Nordic nations apart", "y_label": "points explained on ladder scale", "unit": "", "labels": ["National income", "Social support", "Personal freedom", "Low corruption"], "series": [{"name": "Nordic countries", "data": [2.0, 1.6, 1.1, 0.4]}, {"name": "Other countries", "data": [1.5, 1.2, 0.9, 0.1]}], "note": "Average contribution of each factor to life evaluation scores in 2025."}
```

## long-term stability with minor shifts

If you trace these scores back, this regional dominance is nothing new, though individual rankings have shifted over time (WHR 2026). Finland started at second place in 2011, briefly dipped to seventh in 2012, and then climbed to the top in 2017 (WHR 2026). It has now held the top spot for **nine** consecutive reports, peaking with a score of 7.8 in 2020 (WHR 2026).

Other neighbors have seen more movement (WHR 2026). Iceland began the decade at twentieth place in 2011, rose rapidly, and secured second place in 2025 with a score of **7.5** (WHR 2026). Meanwhile, Norway peaked at first place in 2016 but has steadily slid down to sixth place in 2025, scoring 7.2 (WHR 2026).


## what this data can't tell you

These numbers are based on statistical models rather than direct, individual-level measurements of happiness. The points associated with income, social support, and corruption represent estimated contributions rather than personal experiences. Additionally, because no survey was compiled or published in 2013, the trends for that year remain entirely blank.

trail.task: What are the ranks, life evaluation scores, and countries at the top of the World Happiness Report (whr) in the most recent year available?

queries.sql: SELECT DISTINCT year FROM whr ORDER BY year DESC;

SELECT rank, country, life_evaluation, 
       explained_by_gdp_per_capita, 
       explained_by_social_support, 
       explained_by_healthy_life_expectancy, 
       explained_by_freedom, 
       explained_by_generosity, 
       explained_by_low_corruption, 
       dystopia_plus_residual
FROM whr 
WHERE year = 2025 
ORDER BY rank ASC 
LIMIT 20;

WHERE year = 2025

queries.sql:
SELECT 
  CASE WHEN country IN ('Finland', 'Denmark', 'Iceland', 'Norway', 'Sweden') THEN 'Nordic' ELSE 'Other' END AS group_name,
  COUNT(*) as num_countries,
  AVG(life_evaluation) as avg_life_evaluation,
  AVG(explained_by_gdp_per_capita) as avg_gdp,
  AVG(explained_by_social_support) as avg_social_support,
  AVG(explained_by_healthy_life_expectancy) as avg_health,
  AVG(explained_by_freedom) as avg_freedom,
  AVG(explained_by_generosity) as avg_generosity,
  AVG(explained_by_low_corruption) as avg_low_corruption,
  AVG(dystopia_plus_residual) as avg_dystopia
FROM whr
WHERE year = 2025
GROUP BY group_name;

queries.sql:
SELECT 
  AVG(CASE WHEN group_name = 'Nordic' THEN avg_life_evaluation ELSE NULL END) - AVG(CASE WHEN group_name = 'Other' THEN avg_life_evaluation ELSE NULL END) AS diff_life_evaluation,
  AVG(CASE WHEN group_name = 'Nordic' THEN avg_gdp ELSE NULL END) - AVG(CASE WHEN group_name = 'Other' THEN avg_gdp ELSE NULL END) AS diff_gdp,
  AVG(CASE WHEN group_name = 'Nordic' THEN avg_social_support ELSE NULL END) - AVG(CASE WHEN group_name = 'Other' THEN avg_social_support ELSE NULL END) AS diff_social_support,
  AVG(CASE WHEN group_name = 'Nordic' THEN avg_health ELSE NULL END) - AVG(CASE WHEN group_name = 'Other' THEN avg_health ELSE NULL END) AS diff_health,
  AVG(CASE WHEN group_name = 'Nordic' THEN avg_freedom ELSE NULL END) - AVG(CASE WHEN group_name = 'Other' THEN avg_freedom ELSE NULL END) AS diff_freedom,
  AVG(CASE WHEN group_name = 'Nordic' THEN avg_generosity ELSE NULL END) - AVG(CASE WHEN group_name = 'Other' THEN avg_generosity ELSE NULL END) AS diff_generosity,
  AVG(CASE WHEN group_name = 'Nordic' THEN avg_low_corruption ELSE NULL END) - AVG(CASE WHEN group_name = 'Other' THEN avg_low_corruption ELSE NULL END) AS diff_low_corruption,
  AVG(CASE WHEN group_name = 'Nordic' THEN avg_dystopia ELSE NULL END) - AVG(CASE WHEN group_name = 'Other' THEN avg_dystopia ELSE NULL END) AS diff_dystopia
FROM (
  SELECT 
    CASE WHEN country IN ('Finland', 'Denmark', 'Iceland', 'Norway', 'Sweden') THEN 'Nordic' ELSE 'Other' END AS group_name,
    AVG(life_evaluation) as avg_life_evaluation,
    AVG(explained_by_gdp_per_capita) as avg_gdp,
    AVG(explained_by_social_support) as avg_social_support,
    AVG(explained_by_healthy_life_expectancy) as avg_health,
    AVG(explained_by_freedom) as avg_freedom,
    AVG(explained_by_generosity) as avg_generosity,
    AVG(explained_by_low_corruption) as avg_low_corruption,
    AVG(dystopia_plus_residual) as avg_dystopia
  FROM whr
  WHERE year = 2025
  GROUP BY group_name
);

queries.sql:
SELECT year, country, rank, life_evaluation 
FROM whr 
WHERE country IN ('Denmark', 'Finland', 'Iceland', 'Norway', 'Sweden') 
ORDER BY country, year;

SELECT year, country, rank, life_evaluation 
FROM whr 
WHERE country IN ('Norway', 'Sweden') 
ORDER BY country, year;
SELECT DISTINCT year FROM whr ORDER BY year;

PIVOT (
  SELECT year, country, 
         round(life_evaluation, 3) || ' (#' || rank || ')' AS val
  FROM whr
  WHERE country IN ('Denmark', 'Finland', 'Iceland', 'Norway', 'Sweden')
)
ON country
USING FIRST(val)
ORDER BY year;

SELECT year,
  MAX(CASE WHEN country = 'Denmark' THEN ROUND(life_evaluation, 3) || ' (#' || rank || ')' END) AS Denmark,
  MAX(CASE WHEN country = 'Finland' THEN ROUND(life_evaluation, 3) || ' (#' || rank || ')' END) AS Finland,
  MAX(CASE WHEN country = 'Iceland' THEN ROUND(life_evaluation, 3) || ' (#' || rank || ')' END) AS Iceland,
  MAX(CASE WHEN country = 'Norway' THEN ROUND(life_evaluation, 3) || ' (#' || rank || ')' END) AS Norway,
  MAX(CASE WHEN country = 'Sweden' THEN ROUND(life_evaluation, 3) || ' (#' || rank || ')' END) AS Sweden
FROM whr
WHERE country IN ('Denmark', 'Finland', 'Iceland', 'Norway', 'Sweden')
GROUP BY year
ORDER BY year;

SELECT rank, country, life_evaluation 
FROM whr 
WHERE year = 2025 
ORDER BY rank 
LIMIT 10;
